thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated 502/504 error rates for requests originated from eu-central (observed ~09:07 UTC). Geo-routing trace shows EU-origin traffic being resolved to us-west endpoints by CDN mapping layer.
eng-oncall: Acknowledge. Paging networking and edge team. Any customer tickets?
support-lead: Yep — multiple tickets from Streamly EU and FormCraft EU complaining about slow loads and 504s. They're seeing origins resolved to us-west.
maya: I'm seeing DNS resolution from our public probes — the CDN/edge mapping returned a us-west origin for host api.eu.redwood.net for some EU client ASNs. This started after the edge mapping update at 08:58 UTC.
tom: I noticed a recent change in edge-mapping ruleset 'emap-129' that added a regex to normalize legacy service hostnames: `^(.+)-legacy\.(.+)$` -> backend rewrite. Could be overbroad; maybe it captures eu hosts and maps to fallback bucket.
zara: Joining. Can we capture a sample trace id?
maya: sample trace trace-7c2: client ASN 12345 -> CDN edge -> origin resolved us-west2 -> backend hops to us-west. Header X-Edge-Rule: emap-129.
networking: If emap-129 is misclassifying hostnames, we should immediately disable the rule. But be mindful: rule was added to route legacy traffic away from overloaded EU pools. If we remove it, some legacy traffic may hit EU and cause load. Need quick capacity check.
eng-oncall: Quick plan: 1) Disable emap-129 at edge control plane. 2) Purge CDN mapping cache for eu regional edges. 3) Apply emergency nginx proxy hotfix to honor region pin header before mapping rewrite. 4) Notify customers.
support-lead: Agreed. I'll notify impacted accounts that we're investigating and expect an update in ~15m.
networking: Running disable: 
```
edgectl rule disable --id=emap-129 --by=networking --note="emergency: misrouting EU -> US"
```
incident-bot: edge-bot acknowledged disable job job-9012. Estimated propagation 30s-90s.
eng-oncall: While that's propagating, can someone run `edgectl mapping dump --edge=eu-* --filter=emap-129` so we can see which records were affected?
maya: Dumped mappings: 34 records matched, majority were legacy-service buckets, but three shared hostnames with current services (poor regex anchor). Lists attached to INC-5510.
tom: I'll prepare the nginx patch to short-circuit mapping rewrites when X-Region-Pin header present: 
```
# pseudo
if ($http_x_region_pin) {
  return proxy_pass http://origin-$http_x_region_pin;
}
```
I'll push a canary to eu-edge-2 first.
networking: Disable took effect at 09:12:15 UTC. CDN mapping caches starting to honor previous stable maps.
incident-bot: CDN purge initiated for eu edges by networking.
eng-oncall: Canary nginx patch to eu-edge-2 applied. Telemetry shows that requests with region pin now keep eu origin.
zara: After disable and canary patch, error rate dropped from 1.6% to 0.2% over 5m. Clients reporting faster responses.
support-lead: Support: Letting Streamly EU know we've disabled a faulty mapping rule and are monitoring. They reported service recovery at ~09:15 UTC.
cust-eng: Streamly reports a brief degradation window from 08:58-09:15 UTC, most requests retried successfully. They want an RCA and whether any data loss occurred.
eng-oncall: No data loss detected, mostly timeouts and backend 502s. Estimated affected requests ~4.2k. We'll prepare an incident summary.
networking: Action items we need to follow-up: 1) tighten emap regexes and add unit tests for hostname anchors (ETA 6h), 2) add mapping rule canary stage gating (ETA 4h), 3) add edge-mapping audit logs to show which rules matched each request (ETA 48h).
tom: I'll open a PR for the nginx short-circuit and Terraform for canary rollout gating.
maya: Also recommend reducing mapping TTL at the CDN layer to 60s for experimental rules so misroutes drain faster. I've set experimental TTL change for emap staging. Command used: 
```
edgectl set-ttl --rule=emap-129 --ttl=60 --note="experiment: faster drain for mappings"
```
support-lead: Capturing customer impact: Streamly EU & FormCraft EU reported issues; both have acknowledged our mitigation. Will prepare support pack with logs and timeline.
eng-oncall: Incident classification: P1. Responders: networking, edge, eng-runtime, support. Creating INC-5510.
incident-bot: Incident creation: INC-5510 assigned. Oncall handoff scheduled at 12:00 UTC.
zara: Before we close, let's validate that there are no other edge rules with similar unanchored regexes. I'll run a quick grep across rules.
networking: Found two additional rules using unanchored host regex; flagged in INC-5510.
tom: Can we add a runtime metric: "edge.rule.misroute_detected" when origin region != client region and rule header present? That will give early detection (ETA 72h).
eng-oncall: Noted. Immediate status: mitigated — disabled emap-129, applied nginx patch to honor region pins, CDN purge. Monitoring sliding window.
support-lead: Sending proactive comms now. Draft will say: "We've disabled a mapping rule that incorrectly normalized some hostnames, causing EU traffic to be routed to US origins; mitigation applied and services recovered." Simple, non-technical.
cust-eng: We'll follow-up with affected customers and offer a postmortem call if they want.
incident-bot: Incident marked mitigated at 09:20 UTC by eng-oncall. Please update INC-5510 with all attachments and assign postmortem owners.
eng-oncall: Adding notes to INC-5510, owners: zara (RCA), networking (rule fixes + audits), tom (nginx fix + canary), support-lead (customer comms). Handing off to next oncall — I'll stay reachable for 30m.
support-lead: Good work team. Closing thread for now; reopen if any re-occurrence. :white_check_mark:
